## Jitter: for designers who want the canvas

Per their site as of October 2026, Jitter's pitch is "Design in motion. Now with AI." and it says it "helps creative teams design and ship polished animations at scale". The AI sits inside a design tool: "Describe your idea and let Jitter AI generate editable animations, effects, and variations", plus image to video, one-click resize and translate, and "Magic Import" to "Create hundreds of variations with different copy or assets".

The parts a Hera user would notice, again per Jitter's site and help centre: [...] How it differs from Hera:

 Limited edits after approval. In the draft you can change on-screen words and reorder scenes for free, but spoken lines and length are locked. There's no canvas to nudge an element.
 Three looks, no template library, no saved brand kits. Each look has its own typefaces; your brand arrives as name, logo, colours and product shots, not font files.
 No AI footage in videos made from a description or a look's sample. They're built from type, your screens, graphics, voice, captions and music.
 MP4 only. No GIF, no transparent overlays, no Lottie. If you need an overlay for an edit, Hera and Jitter both list transparent formats.
 No posting. Download the MP4 and post it yourself. [...] By Oakgen TeamPublished 12 min read

Share

The main Hera alternatives in 2026 split by job, not by quality. Pick Jitter if a designer wants to own every frame with a team; Remotion or HyperFrames if you need code, data-driven variants or an agent to build the video; HeyGen if you need a presenter or many languages; Veed if you already have footage and need moving text on it; Oakgen Motion if you want the tool to write, voice and caption a short video around your screens; and Runway only if you want generated footage, which is a different product category. Hera itself remains a good fit for prompt-first motion graphics that you then direct scene by scene.

Quick answer

MotionVid.ai, an AI motion graphics and video generation tool, is the Hera alternative most people running this search actually want: open signup, published pricing from $19/month (500 credits, 60 export minutes), and prompt-made maps, charts, logo ads and explainer scenes. The honest trade-off is that plans are credit-capped, not unlimited, and there are no keyframes: the timeline lets you split, trim and reorder scenes, not hand-tune the animation inside them. If you need hands-on keyframes or a Lottie file for a developer, Jitter is the better pick. On a strict $0 budget, Jitter's free tier is the only free plan here with published limits.
